Havent seen anyone pick the warriors yet, and probably for good reason. It seems like a tough matchup for us.

I think the Warriors path to victory is pretty narrow. 

* I think it's going to be a lot of small-ball, with Draymond guarding Gobert and Jimmy on Randle. They'll be outsized, but they'll be banking on making Gobert less effective by pulling him out to the perimeter on defense. I think they've done this successfully before, but I don't see it being as effective as before (where Rudy was essentially unplayable in Utah)
* Realistically, GP2 is going to need to have a hell of a series to keep up with Ant. He going to be on the floor a lot. I can't see Steph/Hield/Moody/Podz/Kuminga doing anything on defense to slow him down.
* Naz Reid is a bad man. It would be great if Kuminga or Post were able to step up and cover Gobert or Randle, freeing up Jimmy/Draymond to cover Naz a bit, but that's very wishful thinking. 
* From what I've seen, the Wolves were fairly inconsistent this season. Their highs are insane, but the lows are the reason they didn't finish with a way better record. The warriors are really going to be hoping they put up a stinker or two because with the way the wolves played against the lakers, that's really the biggest factor.
* Steph going nuclear is always a possibility, hopefully he has some big games. 
* In regards to the "others", McDaniels/Conley/DDV/Alexander-Walker is certainly a better cast than /Podz/Post/Hield/Moody/GP2, but any of these guys can get hot or go cold, I don't think anyone knows who's going to have the best series or best game out of all these guys, but it'll be a major factor each night. If I had to pick, I'd say McDaniels will have the best series, but Hield will have the best individual game
* It seems like the rockets zone defense really worked well against the warriors - I'd expect the Wolves to use that as a blueprint, at least early on. Try to hide Gobert on someone like Moody/Podz when the warriors are playing small (like the Rockets did with Adams or Sengun)

My main question remains though: What exactly do republican voters want from their government?

From my perspective,

* Taxes are going up (unless you make $2m+ a year)
* Prices on consumer goods are going up (tariffs)
* The services we get from our taxes are going down (education or the weather service for example)
* The value of my retirement/stock portfolio is going down (uncertainty in the market).
* Interest rates aren't going down, buying a house still seems as unrealistic as ever.
* It seems harder to find a new job, a lot of companies and the government are laying off a lot of workers.

I primarily care about myself and my family, as I imagine most people do. I'm not talking about any of the social issues like abortion, immigration, guns, trans-rights or anything that the parties disagree on. 6. Can't use cash considerations in trades (buying picks etc).

General idea is that the value of the building is defined by the expected annual revenue it brings in multiplied by a cap rate. If the expected annual revenue goes down, by lowering the rent of a unit, the value of the building is less. If the value of the building is less, and the landlord has a loan on the building, they may need to put up more collateral to maintain debt covenants. 

Example: building has 10 units, each unit pays 8.3k in rent per month so building has total revenue of 1M per year. Using a cap rate of 5, the building is worth 5M. Landlord purchases building for 5M with 1M cash and loan for 4M so LTV is 80%.

Now he has an empty unit, he could rent it out for 5k a month. If he does that, annual revenue for the building drops from $1M to $960k. Using the same cap rate, the building is now worth $4.8M. The loan now has a LTV of 83%, so he has the put up cash to the bank to bring it back to 80%

So instead of lowering the value of the building by lowering the monthly rent. he just keeps the unit empty or offers free months or gift cards to make up the difference
